content:
Apple has acquired certain assets of SigScalr, the developer of the observability application SigLens, and has hired its employees. Details below.

Apple acquires part of SigScalr's business

Under the EU's Digital Markets Act, Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, ByteDance, Meta and Microsoft must notify the European Commission of any acquisitions or other regulated actions, and the Commission publishes transaction details on its website.

Today, the site updated with a new acquisition by Apple, involving SigScalr, the developer of the observability platform SigLens.

SigLens is an open-source observability platform designed to help developers collect, search and analyse logs, metrics and trace data generated by applications and infrastructure. SigScalr positioned it as a more efficient alternative to services like Splunk, Datadog and Elasticsearch.

Regarding this acquisition, Apple told the EU:

The acquisition was listed as completed on March 12. Since then, SigScalr's official website has ceased to operate, and SigLens's main GitHub repository has also been archived and set to read-only.

In the archival notice, the developers stated:

Today, we officially archive this project. First and foremost, thank you. 🙏 This project started as a mere idea, and it grew into what it is today thanks to the support of our community members. Your pull requests, bug reports, feature suggestions, stars, blog posts, tweets, and words of encouragement made this project what it is. Your trust in us, and the time you invested, meant the world to us.

What do you think Apple will do with this acquisition? Let us know in the comments.
